name: Navigate nodes, folders and files
summary: Jev chooses observed navigation candidates; the system reads bounded sources and retains the path and evidence.

steps.label: Offer a scoped starting frontier
steps.human:
Expose permitted observed starting nodes/relationships or repository folders/files from the selected plan and pinned source. Include identifiers, types, path/edge meaning and source locators. Do not infer a complete call graph from file existence. Bind reads to immutable revision bytes/materialization, or explicitly identify working-tree bytes with content hashes. A commit label alone does not pin changing filesystem content. Do not conflate these modes.

I/O boundary: The existing Scope limits allowed reads. It does not serialize candidate folder entries or assert a semantic dependency graph.

steps.label: Choose the next navigation step
steps.human:
Choose one or more offered node/edge neighbours, directories, files or bounded excerpts that may answer the ORIGINAL question. Choose continue, return evidence, switch method, clarify or stop. Never invent candidate IDs/paths or perform reads.

Graph navigation and repository navigation are distinct offered modes. Select among observed candidates; no arbitrary Cypher or unrestricted filesystem exploration.

steps.label: Validate the selected frontier
steps.human:
Check selected IDs/paths against observed candidates, pinned revision, allowed relationships/read roots and remaining limits. Apply visited/attempt history to prevent cycles and identical no-progress reads. Reject escaped, unavailable or stale candidates without broadening scope. Enforce configured scan-entry, depth, elapsed-time, read-count and byte bounds, not merely a returned-candidate cap. Graph relation/mapping availability must come from the actual serving manifest. A valid return/switch/clarify/stop decision bypasses reading and goes to retention, preserving its original decision and history.

I/O boundary: Kernel scope is reusable authority. It cannot by itself prove a chosen path was observed or a changing file was pinned.

steps.label: Read nodes or code locations
steps.human:
For an accepted selection, enumerate the bounded next graph neighbours or folder entries, or read the selected node/file excerpt. Preserve edge direction/path, source/revision, locator, limit/truncation and execution outcome. This is actual system traversal, not Jev generation.

Charge each read to the existing run budget and record visited identities; matching resume must not repeat completed reads. A file/folder relationship is navigation evidence, not proof of a semantic dependency. Returned subsets do not prove full folder/graph coverage, absence or exact counts; disclose truncation and unresolved boundaries.

I/O boundary: The existing graph-result projection is only a reusable subset. A folder read and its next frontier are still unbound; no generated traversal is claimed.

steps.label: Retain history and return or resume
steps.human:
Checkpoint visited/frontier identities, attempts, evidence and remaining budget with the same question/scope/source. Route the bounded decision: continue at [frontier selection](docs/product-truth/flows/leafcutter/retrieval-source-traversal.flow.json#frontier); otherwise return separate outcomes to [shared comparison](docs/product-truth/flows/leafcutter/retrieve-project-knowledge.flow.json#compare). After comparison and advisory recording, a method switch returns to [main planning](docs/product-truth/flows/leafcutter/retrieve-project-knowledge.flow.json#plan), not an untracked recursive search.

I/O boundary: Known envelope only: no strict nested traversal DTO is asserted. This illustrative blocked result has no checkpoint, so it does not imply traversal already resumes.

provenance.note:
Proposed adaptive traversal — not built
This dedicated method refines the existing retrieval journey. It describes Jev frontier choice and System traversal with multi-method return routes. Existing bounded graph operations and native repository retrieval are reusable primitives, not proof that this adaptive node/folder navigation loop is wired. No runtime, provider or source publication occurs in this design task.

Architecture evidence: existing graph neighbour/recipe operations and native allowlisted file enumeration/locators are primitives. No public Jev frontier-navigation or directory-listing contract is currently exposed. A proposed typed enumerate-frontier/read-selected adapter must preserve visited IDs and scan bounds. Native worktree reads are not immutable Git reads merely because a revision label is attached. This draft does not claim a complete code/call/import graph.

Added source-bound field/type/requiredness/default metadata and explicitly illustrative JSON projections. Preserved topology, actor ownership, realization and AC status. Non-JSON artifacts and genuinely undefined proposed interfaces remain explicit.
